response:
Reflection on gen-0 evidence: (i) rank-**difference** structures (Self-Funded R&D Intensity) delivered both cross-sectional and portfolio evidence, while every **MUL-of-ranks** and **SIGN-conditioned** construction produced flat or wrong-signed FF5 alphas — products concentrate the extremes in one theme and destroy monotonicity; (ii) coverage was capped at 0.06–0.13, because cash-flow-statement financing items (sstk, dltis, prstkc) are sparse — balance-sheet financing proxies (csho, dltt, dlc) should repair this; (iii) the winner's FF5 alpha t-stat (1.70) lagged its FMB t-stat (4.81), which is the signature of an industry tilt (R&D intensity is an industry characteristic), motivating industry-neutral conditioning. This batch therefore keeps additive/difference structures, repairs coverage, tests industry neutralization, and adds two genuinely new channels (per-share intangible capital delivery; financing-capacity state rather than flow).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Dilution-Adjusted R&D Intensity
EXPRESSION: SUB(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible investment sustained without shareholder dilution is productive innovation, whereas intangible spending accompanied by share-count expansion reflects market-timed equity funding; measuring dilution from shares outstanding rather than the cash-flow-statement issuance item captures the same economics for the whole cross-section.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-0 winner used the same rank-difference logic but was restricted to firms reporting sstk, capping coverage at 0.127 and thinning the extreme portfolios, which is the most likely cause of its weak alpha t-stat relative to its 4.8 FMB t-stat. Share-count growth is available for essentially all firms and captures all dilution channels (secondary offerings, equity-financed deals, option exercise), so this isolates the coverage design choice while holding the mechanism fixed.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Industry-Neutral Self-Funded Innovation
EXPRESSION: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Within an industry, the firm that funds its intangible program internally rather than through equity and debt issuance is the one whose innovation is genuinely value-creating; across industries the same comparison mostly reproduces sector R&D norms and financing conventions, which FF5 factors already span.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-0 winner's large FMB slope but weak FF5 alpha t-stat suggests the long-short leg was a pharma/tech versus financials-utilities bet whose systematic component is absorbed by the factor model. Ranking both themes inside industry should preserve the cross-sectional slope while converting it into a cleaner, better-diversified spread, and it also tests total external financing (equity plus debt) rather than equity alone.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Net-Financing-Free Knowledge Capital
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), SUMRANK(NEG(GROWTH(csho, 1)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(dltt, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: A deep accumulated knowledge stock that was built while both equity and debt financing were shrinking identifies self-financing innovators whose intangible capital the market underprices; the same knowledge stock built on simultaneous equity and debt expansion reflects externally subsidized, overvaluation-driven investment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Gen-0's Payout-Backed Knowledge Capital tested the same idea but proxied "no external funding" with repurchases and dividends, which selects large mature payers and gave a negative alpha; net changes in shares and in total debt measure contraction of external capital directly and include young non-payers. Five-year cumulative R&D captures the intangible state rather than a noisy annual flow, and equal-weight nested SUMRANK avoids the multiplicative structures that failed in gen 0.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Intangible Capital Delivered Per Share
EXPRESSION: GROWTH(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3)), csho), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: The only intangible investment that matters to an incumbent shareholder is the amount surviving dilution, so growth in intangible capital per share separates financing that actually bought innovation from financing that merely transferred claims; firms increasing intangible capital per share earn positive abnormal returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This changes the interaction from an additive comparison of two ranks to a single per-share intensity, so the financing theme enters as the deflator of the intangible theme rather than as a competing score — a structurally different test of the same story. Combining booked intangibles with three-year cumulative R&D gives one economically complete intangible capital measure, and the one-year growth makes the signal about newly delivered capital rather than about the level of R&D intensity.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Externally Financed Intangible Acquisition
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(DELTA(intan, 1), at), RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at))
HYPOTHESIS: Balance-sheet intangibles grow mainly through acquisitions, and when that growth coincides with heavy equity and debt issuance the firm is paying up for other companies' intangibles with cheap outside capital, which predicts subsequent write-downs and low returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Gen-0's goodwill version had a coherent FMB slope (-2.80) but a dead long-short leg, consistent with the MUL structure making the signal near-zero for the vast majority of firms and leaving the portfolio extremes unstable. Replacing the product with an additive SUMRANK gives a continuous, well-populated score, and using total intangibles rather than goodwill alone broadens the acquired-intangible measure.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Innovation With Unused Debt Capacity
EXPRESSION: SUB(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Because intangible assets are poor collateral, an R&D-intensive firm that has chosen to carry little debt retains real financing capacity and is not investing under distress pressure; the market underprices such firms relative to intangible-heavy firms whose innovation is already levered.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: All prior proposals used financing flows; this one uses the financing state (stock of debt), so it tests whether the interaction operates through capital-structure capacity rather than through the timing of new issues. It also has near-universal coverage because it needs only xrd, dltt, dlc and at, which addresses the sparsity that plagued the flow-based archive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
